socfpga_spi.h

SPI hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Types
spi_xfer_status_t

Defines the standard return and completion status codes for SPI driver operations, particularly used to indicate hardware states during asynchronous callback execution.

Values
SPI_SUCCESS

The full-duplex SPI transaction completed without any hardware faults.

SPI_WR_ERROR

A hardware error occurred while pushing data to the Transmit FIFO (TXFIFO).

SPI_RD_ERROR

A hardware error occurred while pulling data from the Receive FIFO (RXFIFO), such as an underflow/overflow.

SPI_XFER_ERROR

A general bus error or timeout occurred during the transaction.

spi_mode_t

Defines the physical SPI bus clock framing formats, dictating the Clock Polarity (CPOL) and Clock Phase (CPHA) used by the master to shift and sample data bits.

Values
SPI_MODE0

CPOL = 0 (Clock idles low), CPHA = 0 (Data sampled on leading edge).

SPI_MODE1

CPOL = 0 (Clock idles low), CPHA = 1 (Data sampled on trailing edge).

SPI_MODE2

CPOL = 1 (Clock idles high), CPHA = 0 (Data sampled on leading edge).

SPI_MODE3

CPOL = 1 (Clock idles high), CPHA = 1 (Data sampled on trailing edge).

spi_ioctl_t

Input/Output Control commands used to modify or retrieve the internal state and configuration of the SPI Master controller dynamically at runtime.

Values
SPI_SET_CONFIG

Programs the hardware baud rate divisor and clock phase/polarity. Expects a pointer to spi_cfg_t.

SPI_GET_CONFIG

Reads the current active baud rate and mode from the hardware registers. Expects a pointer to spi_cfg_t.

SPI_GET_TX_NBYTES

Retrieves the exact number of bytes successfully pushed to the TXFIFO in the last operation. Expects a uint16_t pointer.

SPI_GET_RX_NBYTES

Retrieves the exact number of bytes successfully pulled from the RXFIFO in the last operation. Expects a uint16_t pointer.

spi_cfg_t

Configuration structure used with the SPI_SET_CONFIG and SPI_GET_CONFIG IOCTLs to define the primary electrical and timing characteristics of the SPI bus.

Types
spi_handle_t

An opaque software handle representing an active connection to a specific SPI Master hardware instance. It encapsulates the base MMIO address, current buffer pointers, transfer sizes, and synchronization primitives required for driver state.

spi_callback_t

Function pointer signature for the application-level interrupt service routine (ISR) callback. This is invoked when an asynchronous SPI transfer completes, or when the hardware flags a critical FIFO error.

Parameters
status

The hardware completion status of the background transfer.

pparam

An opaque user context pointer registered via spi_set_callback.

spi_open
spi_handle_t spi_open(
uint32_t 
instance
)

Initializes a specific SPI Master hardware block. This function un-gates the peripheral clock via the SoC Clock Manager, brings the IP out of reset via the Reset Manager, and prepares the internal software descriptor for use.

Parameters
instance
uint32_t

The zero-indexed hardware instance number (e.g., 0 for SPI0, 1 for SPI1).

Returns

A valid spi_handle_t on success; NULL if the instance is out of bounds or the hardware fails to initialize.

Registers a user-defined function to be executed upon the completion of asynchronous SPI transfers (spi_transfer_async).

Parameters

spi_callback_t

The function pointer to invoke upon transfer completion or error.

spi_ioctl
int32_t spi_ioctl(
spi_handle_t const 
hspi,
spi_ioctl_t 
cmd,
void *const 
buf
)

Provides a standardized interface for configuring hardware parameters or querying the state of the SPI controller without needing specialized functions.

Parameters
hspi
spi_handle_t const

The active SPI instance handle.

cmd
spi_ioctl_t

The specific control command from spi_ioctl_t.

buf
void* const

Pointer to the data payload associated with the command (e.g., spi_cfg_t for configuration, or a uint16_t for reading byte counts).

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if arguments are invalid or pointers are NULL.  -EBUSY if a hardware transfer is currently active and the configuration cannot be changed safely.

spi_transfer_sync
int32_t spi_transfer_sync(
spi_handle_t const 
hspi,
uint8_t *const 
txbuf,
uint8_t *const 
rxbuf,
uint16_t 
nbytes
)

Initiates a blocking, full-duplex SPI transaction. The driver writes data into the Transmit FIFO (TXFIFO) and polls the Receive FIFO (RXFIFO) to read the incoming shifted data. Because SPI is fundamentally full-duplex, the hardware master clock is driven for exactly `nbytes`.

If only a write is desired, the user must pass a valid `txbuf` and NULL for `rxbuf` (the driver will silently discard incoming bytes). If only a read is desired, `txbuf` should contain dummy bytes (usually 0xFF) and `rxbuf` must be valid.

Parameters
hspi
spi_handle_t const

The active SPI instance handle.

txbuf
uint8_t* const

Pointer to the transmission payload buffer (or dummy data for a read).

rxbuf
uint8_t* const

Pointer to the destination buffer to hold incoming data.

nbytes
uint16_t

The exact number of bytes to shift across the bus.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if arguments are invalid.  -EBUSY if another operation is actively occupying the bus.  -EIO on a hardware timeout or FIFO fault.

spi_transfer_async
int32_t spi_transfer_async(
spi_handle_t const 
hspi,
uint8_t *const 
txbuf,
uint8_t *const 
rxbuf,
uint16_t 
nbytes
)

Initiates a non-blocking, full-duplex SPI transaction utilizing hardware interrupts. The driver primes the internal state machines and writes the first chunk of data into the TXFIFO. Control is immediately returned to the caller.  The internal ISR handles refilling the TXFIFO and draining the RXFIFO as hardware watermark interrupts fire.

Parameters
hspi
spi_handle_t const

The active SPI instance handle.

txbuf
uint8_t* const

Pointer to the transmission payload buffer. Must remain valid in memory until the callback fires.

rxbuf
uint8_t* const

Pointer to the destination buffer. Must remain valid in memory until the callback fires.

nbytes
uint16_t

The exact number of bytes to shift across the bus.

Returns

0 if the transfer was successfully queued and hardware started.  -EINVAL if arguments are invalid.  -EBUSY if the bus or internal state machine is currently locked by another transfer.

spi_close
int32_t spi_close(
spi_handle_t const 
hspi
)

Safely deconstructs the software context for an active SPI controller. This disables the Master Enable bit in the hardware, masks all interrupts, clears pending FIFOs, and releases the handle memory.

Parameters
hspi
spi_handle_t const

The active SPI instance handle to shut down.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the handle is invalid or already closed.

spi_cancel
int32_t spi_cancel(
spi_handle_t const 
hspi
)

Attempts to halt an ongoing asynchronous operation. Note: Aborting an active SPI transaction mid-shift can corrupt bus states and leave slave devices desynchronized. For this bare-metal driver implementation, cancellation is unsupported.

Parameters
hspi
spi_handle_t const

The active SPI instance handle.

Returns

Always returns -ENOSYS (Function not implemented).

spi_select_slave
int32_t spi_select_slave(
spi_handle_t const 
hspi,
uint32_t 
ss
)

Configures the Slave Select Enable Register (SER). The SPI master hardware can natively control multiple distinct Slave Select (NSS) output lines. This function routes the active master output to a specific physical slave pin.

Parameters
hspi
spi_handle_t const

The active SPI instance handle.

ss
uint32_t

The zero-indexed hardware slave select line to assert (e.g., 0, 1, 2).

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the requested slave select line exceeds hardware capabilities.
